Graduate Programs
The Computer Science department currently offers three graduate programs:
Graduate Certificate in Secure Cyber Operations
Master of Science (MS) in Computer Science
PhD EAS (Engineering and Applied Science) with Computer Science Concentration
If you would like additional information on any of the graduate programs, click the button below.
Request More Info
Graduate Certificate in Secure Cyber Operations
This certificate was developed as part of the state-wide cybersecurity education initiative between the Idaho universities and Idaho National Laboratory to provide students who have completed a bachelor’s degree with sufficient skills to obtain an Idaho cyber operations job. The certificate requires 12 credit hours, can be completed in one year, and dovetails with the MSCS.
If you are interested in this certificate, please contact David Beard ( beard@isu.edu )
Graduate Secure Cyber Operations Certificate requirements and application info
Master of Science in Computer Science
A Masters in Science (MS) in Computer Science (CS) develops and advances a student's knowledge and skills in computer science in particular focused areas. This graduate program develops the students' critical thinking, investigatory, and expository skills. MS students will learn the foundations of computer science theory and application and the interaction between the two. Students will also get the opportunity to choose a thesis-based track and learn research methodologies for addressing an important problem and presenting proposed solutions both orally and in writing.
MS in CS requirements and admission information
Catalog
PhD in EAS with Computer Science Concentration
The Computer Science (CS) department offers PhD in Engineering and Applied Science (EAS) with CS concentration. In this PhD program, a student will develop intellectual and research skills by pursuing original and impactful research under close supervision of a CS professor. A PhD student will also learn to write and present scholarly articles through dissemination of their PhD research results in the form of peer-reviewed scientific publications. Students will develop academic background and breadth of knowledge through coursework, while original and impactful contributions to the existing literature and state-of-the-art with new knowledge and tools constitute the core of the PhD program.
PhD in Engineering and Applied Science (EAS) with CS Concentration

Financial Assistance
There are limited opportunities for financial assistance in terms of Graduate Assistantship (GA) and Scholarship for Service (SFS).
Graduate (Research/Teaching) Assistantships
Limited financial assistance is available to graduate students in the form of Graduate Research Assistantship (GRA) and Graduate Teaching Assistantship (GTA). For GRA, students/applicants are encouraged to first find a professor who will agree to hire them as a GRA and advise their thesis research. Once you find one, you will have to work with the professor to complete the necessary paperwork including the following Graduate Assistantship Application Form.
A GTA award typically covers the tuition fees and also pays a handsome stipend during the fall and spring semesters only (excluding summer). GTA positions are allocated based on availability as well as on a competitive and need basis typically after an applicant is admitted. The CS department's criteria for the selection of GTA's are available here:
GTA-Allocation-Criteria-CS
Students/Applicants seeking GTA positions need to apply using the Graduate Assistantship Application Form listed below. The application form includes instructions about how to submit the application package and also identifies the required supporting documents to be attached to the application. Existing/current ISU students should attach only their resume/CV with the application form while the CV must include their current CGPA, academic advisor’s name, a list of all academic degrees with CGPA, and the awarding institution's name.
Existing GTAs who are applying for GTA again must also fill up the following GTA-Reporting Form. New applicants (who are not currently GTAs) must also fill up the following New Applicant’s Supplementary Form. GTA applications are accepted only in the Spring semester until February 28. Incomplete applications may not be considered.
Graduate Assistantship Application form (all applicants must complete and submit)
New Applicant’s Supplementary Form (must be filled by all new applicants who are not currently GTAs)
GTA-Reporting Form (must be filled by the existing GTAs only, who are re-applying for continuation to the next academic year)
Scholarship for Service (SFS)
Graduate students who are US citizens (or lawful permanent residents) and interested in cybersecurity, may pursue Scholarship for Service (SFS) opportunity. Selected students (Scholars) receive a full tuition scholarship and up to $37,000 annual stipend for two years, in exchange for which recipients agree to work for the U.S. Government for two years after graduation. For more information including instructions and deadline for application, please visit -
https://www.isu.edu/niatec/
Application Deadline
The computer science graduate program (MS/PhD) admits new students in the fall semester only. The department’s deadline for receiving your complete application (including reference letters) is February 28, which means one needs to submit a complete application weeks before this date to allow the admission office to complete the initial screening and forward the complete application (along with the reference letters) to the department for assessment.
Submit application materials using the Admission Application Portal.
